summary: Friday's pass found a codebase with strong stated fail-closed quality doctrine but two concrete places where implementation still turns an inability to judge into permission to continue. The third-capture subsystem has a post-render QA exception path that explicitly passes clips, while the flagship novelty gate reports no stale spans when duration probing fails. Separately, the auto-editor can retain an impact cue after removing the replay that owned it. Longer term, third_capture's proof ledger is useful provenance but is not itself an integrity-checked artifact: the displayed command is caller-supplied and the ledger is saved/loaded as ordinary mutable JSON without verification. The latest evidence also shows production remains materially unhealthy (0/4 explainers and 2/6 trending on the latest judged day, with trending repair incomplete after 10 attempts), but those operational symptoms were not re-filed where existing settled/open-backlog items already cover their causes.

findings.title: Third-capture QA passes clips when QA itself crashes
findings.observation: The full review gate promises NEVER to raise, but its outer exception handler appends 'qa internal error (failed open)' and then sets verdict='pass'. Any unexpected probe, contact-sheet, vision, or local QA failure inside that try block therefore authorizes the clip instead of withholding it.
findings.proposal: Fail closed on QA-internal errors: return verdict='fail' (or an explicit quarantine/error verdict that every caller treats as non-publishable), preserve the exception text as evidence, and add a regression test that forces an internal QA exception and proves the clip cannot advance.
findings.evidence: third_capture/clip_qa.py, review(): the docstring says 'QA-internal error fails open'; the outer except appends 'qa internal error (failed open)' and assigns verdict = 'pass'.

findings.title: Dropping an overlength replay leaves its whoosh cue behind
findings.observation: build_edl() adds a 'whoosh' SFX cue at the start of an appended replay. If the output exceeds 52 seconds, it removes replay segments but filters cues only where cue[1] != 'riser'. The replay never added a riser, so its whoosh survives after the replay segment is gone and can fire at the old end-of-timeline position.
findings.proposal: When removing replay segments, remove the cue(s) owned by that replay using the replay start time or explicit cue ownership instead of filtering the unrelated 'riser' label; add a unit test for an over-cap EDL with replay enabled.
findings.evidence: third_capture/auto_edit.py, build_edl(): the replay branch appends (out_t, 'whoosh'); the subsequent max_out cleanup deletes kind=='replay' segments but removes only cues whose label is 'riser'.

findings.title: Hard novelty gate treats probe failure as a clean video
findings.observation: DIRECTOR.md defines NOVELTY as gate 0, says it is enforced rather than advised, and says a stale span rejects the render. novelty_check() obtains duration with ffprobe inside a broad exception handler, but on any exception it returns an empty list. Empty means no stale spans, so a broken/missing probe silently satisfies the hard gate.
findings.proposal: Represent 'could not evaluate novelty' separately from 'no novelty violations' and make the director fail closed when gate 0 cannot run. Persist the probe failure in the scorecard/report so a tooling outage is distinguishable from a genuinely clean film, with a test that forces ffprobe failure.
findings.evidence: data_learning/DIRECTOR.md, 'The hardline rule' and scorecard gate 0 require novelty enforcement; scripts/no_dull_beats.py, novelty_check(), catches any duration-probe exception and immediately returns [].

findings.title: Proof-mode ledger is evidence without an integrity boundary
findings.observation: capture_cli.py describes itself as the truthfulness layer whose replay and measured claims come from recorded artifacts. It hashes files that callers explicitly record, but the displayed shell_line is accepted directly from the caller, and save_ledger()/load_ledger() simply serialize and deserialize ordinary JSON. Nothing in this module binds argv, terminal events, shell_line, measurements, and referenced file hashes into one identity that a downstream renderer can verify before replay.
findings.proposal: Evolve proof mode toward a content-addressed proof manifest: derive or validate the displayed command from argv, hash a canonical ledger payload containing argv/events/measurements/artifact hashes, and require downstream composition to verify that identity before treating a capture as proof. Keep human-readable JSON, but make tampering or accidental post-capture edits detectable rather than trusted by convention.
findings.evidence: third_capture/capture_cli.py: capture() stores shell_line as shell_line or ' '.join(argv); record_file() hashes selected files; save_ledger() writes json.dumps(asdict(cap)); load_ledger() only json.loads() the file with no ledger-integrity verification.
